message.content: {"answer": "E", "option_text": "Silicosis with nodular opacities", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, predominantly upper and mid-zone reticulo-nodular opacities (indicated by blue arrows) without cavitation, honeycombing, or massive mediastinal widening. This pattern of discrete nodular opacities in the upper lobes is the classic radiographic presentation of silicosis (a form of pneumoconiosis), distinguishing it from the basal predominance of fibrosis (D) or the cavitary lesions of TB (A). While sarcoidosis (B) also affects upper zones, the specific description of 'nodular opacities' aligns most directly with silicosis among the choices."}
